official.description_text:
Postdoc in modelling and digital twin development
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences in Chemistry, Biotechnology and Health
Job description
Would you like to build a physics-based model and a digital twin of how bio-based materials are pressed and dried? We are looking for a postdoc at the Department of Fibre and Polymer Technology at KTH and the Wallenberg Wood Science Center.
In a Formas-funded project together with Hitachi Energy and Nordic Seafarm, we develop knowledge and tools to reduce the energy used in the dewatering and drying of bio-based materials. Your role is to develop a robust numerical model of mechanical dewatering and subsequent thermal drying and to advance it into a validated digital twin of the process.
You will work within a continuum porous-media framework – Darcy flow coupled to heat transfer with phase change – and implement the model in existing codes and/or COMSOL, including AI-tools. You will calibrate and validate the model against experimental data, demonstrate a digital twin using industrial or lab data, and work closely with an experimental postdoc and industrial partners.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Documented scientific expertise in numerical modelling and simulation of coupled physical phenomena, demonstrated through publications.
Experience of finite element or finite volume methods and scientific programming, e.g. Python, MATLAB, C++ or Fortran.
Very good command of English, spoken and written, as it is required in the daily work.
As a person you are independent, take initiative and have a strong ability to collaborate in an interdisciplinary environment.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Experience of COMSOL Multiphysics or equivalent multiphysics simulation software.
Experience of modelling dewatering, drying or wet pressing of pulp, paper or fibre networks.
Experience of calibrating and validating models against experimental data, or of digital twins and reduced-order models.
Teaching abilities.
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

ai.summary: Postdoc in numerical modelling and digital-twin development for mechanical dewatering and thermal drying of bio-based materials, using continuum porous-media framework (Darcy flow, heat transfer with phase change). Role involves finite-element/finite-volume implementation in COMSOL and Python, calibration against experimental data, and collaboration with experimental postdoc and industrial partners.

thematic_fit.rationale: The posting focuses on continuum mechanics, multiphysics modelling, and digital-twin implementation for materials processes. The researcher's focus is human-centred XR, spatial learning, and collaborative immersive interaction. The mention of 'digital twin' in the researcher's background refers to a campus XR simulation for orientation; here it refers to a physical-process simulation model. Thematic overlap is superficial and misleading.

methodological_fit.rationale: The researcher has software development experience (Unity, C#, multiplayer networking) and design-science methodology. This position requires numerical modelling (finite-element methods), scientific programming (Python, MATLAB, C++, COMSOL), and physics-based model calibration. While both involve software, the methodological foundations differ: the researcher builds interactive systems and evaluates human outcomes; this role develops simulation and physical models. Some programming overlap exists, but application domains are distinct.

growth_value.rationale: Developing numerical-modelling and COMSOL expertise is not aligned with the researcher's stated capability gaps. The researcher targets spatial cognition, immersive-system design, and collaborative learning evaluation. Numerical continuum mechanics and digital-twin modelling of industrial processes would introduce technical depth orthogonal to the target identity. Limited growth value for human-centred XR research.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is reputable and the Wallenberg Wood Science Center adds prestige. However, the Department of Fibre and Polymer Technology and industrial partners (Hitachi Energy, Nordic Seafarm) are outside HCI and immersive systems ecosystems. This position does not align with target institutions (Aalto, TU Delft) or research communities focused on human-centred design. No pathway to target identity.

eligibility_flags: Requires completed PhD by employment start; researcher has MSc in progress (thesis stage).
Requires demonstrated expertise in numerical modelling and coupled-physics simulation; researcher's background is in interactive software and HCI, not computational physics.
Requires experience with COMSOL Multiphysics or equivalent; researcher has no stated experience with finite-element or multiphysics software.
risks: Does not meet doctoral degree requirement at application time.
Significant methodological gap: researcher is trained in HCI and design-science research; this role requires computational physics and numerical-analysis expertise.
No background in finite-element methods, continuum mechanics, COMSOL, or multiphysics modelling; domain requires substantial retraining.
Moves research trajectory away from human-centred systems and spatial cognition toward industrial process modelling.
Python experience alone does not compensate for missing physics and modelling foundations.
